result:
**Verdict: CONDITIONAL GO.** The continuation is well-posed, the information boundary is intact, and the claims ceiling (PASS_MASS_MAP_FEASIBILITY_ONLY) is proportionate to what a 13-field fit with reused development fields can support. Three essential pre-launch corrections below; everything else is deferrable.

## Q-GOAL

Sound and honest. The single-field 5000-step pass established only that the network can fit one native decomposition, and the bundle says so plainly ("potentially memorization"). The next question — can a shared model predict role-mass maps across multiple native fields and on spatially disjoint fields it never trained on — is the correct next rung, and it is genuinely needed before any observation-conditioning work is worth designing. The bundle correctly keeps the final science route (CF4 posterior → ICs → forward zoom) out of scope and states that neither outcome here supplies member COM velocities or inverse member-to-field conditioning. The retained 300-step failure and the explicit "development fields are not an independent test set" caveat keep the record honest.

## Q-LEAN

Compliant. One continuation, no new model family, frozen hyperparameters/loss/optimizer state, reused runner/tests/baseline/evaluation, one new output directory, one focused schedule regression, no new gate framework, no intermediate checkpoint selection. The with/without-fixture0 dual aggregate from the same 13 rows is the right lightweight answer to pretraining contamination — but see correction E1, because as written it is report-only. The refusal of pilot-stops mid-fit is acceptable given the user has explicitly prioritized one useful budget over incremental extensions, and the endpoint-reproduction gate before the first new step is the one restart check that actually matters.

## Feasibility

Plausible with two watch items:

- **Runtime.** 13000 × 0.48 s ≈ 104 min is extrapolated from the single-field run, which (per the bundle) did not apply the 48-group augmentation. Rotating/reflecting ten 128³ channels per update, plus cycling 13 fields through the loader, can plausibly push per-update cost to 0.6–0.7 s, which lands at 130–150 min against a 150-min learning cutoff. The INCONCLUSIVE_BUDGET classification makes an overrun honest rather than misleading, so this is not a blocker, but it is the most likely non-PASS outcome. If augmentation can run on-GPU or be applied as an indexing transform rather than a data copy, the margin recovers.
- **Host memory.** The 3.336 GiB observed peak is single-field. Thirteen resident 128³ multi-channel FP32 fields add roughly 1–1.5 GiB if the loader caches them all. That likely still fits 6 GiB, but it is an untested regime — see E2.

The GPU envelope (2.244 GiB observed vs 20 GiB retained), FP32, gradient clip, and partition list are all reused and fine. The failure taxonomy (INCONCLUSIVE_BUDGET vs INCOMPLETE_EXECUTION vs scientific NO-GO) is correctly separated.

## Essential pre-launch corrections

**E1 — Bind the training acceptance gate to a declared aggregate.** The v2 criterion "mean training L1 each of 4 roles ≤ 0.8 baseline" is ambiguous between the 13-field mean and the 12-field mean excluding pretrained fixture0, and "pretraining alone must not dominate the claim" is currently unfalsifiable report-only language. Declare before launch that the gate is evaluated on the 12 non-pretrained fields, with the 13-field aggregate reported as secondary. Otherwise a memorized fixture0 row can drag a 13-field mean across the threshold and the PASS label overstates generalization.

**E2 — One-line memory accounting for the 13-field loader.** Before launch, state whether the runner holds all 13 augmented fields resident or loads per update, and confirm the resident-set estimate fits the 6 GiB request. A startup assertion or a documented arithmetic estimate suffices; no diagnostic series.

**E3 — Cover the vector-channel augmentation with one deterministic test.** The 48 signed rotations/reflections over velocity/dispersion/observer channels are a new code path (changed data exposure is intentional; the six existing tests predate it). A sign error in reflecting velocity components would silently corrupt all 13000 updates and would be indistinguishable from a scientific NO-GO at evaluation. If an existing test already verifies that a reflection flips the corresponding velocity components and transforms the observer features consistently, cite it; if not, add exactly one fixed-input transform test. This is the single highest-value correction in the bundle.

## Deferred (correctly or acceptably)

Per-field-adequacy of 1000 exposures (bundle already disclaims it as an engineering choice); independent held-out test fields; role-assignment multimodality diagnostics; M33 separate-peak analysis; checkpoint-selection studies; all observation-conditioning machinery (joint F,S law, p(E|F,O), COM/stellar offsets, priors); any diffusion repair or observed-LG job. None of these should be pulled forward.

## MW/M31/M33 identification on NEW fields without oracle labels

The mechanism is coherent: at inference the network sees only total moments and coarse observer features, and identification is the network's own role-channel output, anchored (if at all) by the observer features — presumably learning "MW is the halo at the observer" and disambiguating M31/M33 by mass and geometry. The evaluation compares against native labels that exist for the development fields, so a systematic MW/M31 role swap would fail the median-overlap ≥ 0.5 gate and be recorded as NO-GO rather than silently averaged away. That is the right behavior for a feasibility gate. The bundle's own caveat is correct and should be preserved verbatim in the report: deterministic mean maps cannot represent assignment multimodality, so a PASS here shows the deterministic readout works on these fields, not that role identification is well-posed in general. Note also that with only 3 development fields, the median criteria tolerate one bad field — acceptable for feasibility, but the per-field rows must appear in the report so that tolerance is visible.

## Unresolved / shared-cell M33

Handled acceptably. Fractional role targets are well-defined even when M33 shares a cell with M31, so the L1/mass criteria remain meaningful without a separate-peak rule, and refusing a waived criterion is the right call — a network that can only find M33 when it is spatially resolved should fail this gate. The 16 positive-target availability assertions are the necessary guard that no evaluation field silently lacks an M33 target. The one thing the plan should ensure the report states per-field: whether M33 is cell-resolved in each of the 3 development fields, because an M33 PASS driven entirely by resolved cases would need that context to be interpreted honestly.

## SAME-field observation conditioning

The boundary is clean and the bundle polices it correctly: the mean-field OOD ablation is labeled sensitivity evidence only, and the explicit list of missing machinery (joint field–substructure law, selection model, COM/stellar offsets, priors) with the statement that "LG constraints must eventually change the SAME total field, not just its role labels" is exactly the right framing. Nothing in the acceptance criteria or PASS label leaks toward a conditioning or posterior claim. No correction needed; carry the paragraph into the final report unchanged.

## Proportionality of budget and claims

Proportionate on both sides. One 3-hour single-GPU job against a question that gates the entire downstream design is cheap; the refusal to sweep seeds/LR or extend budgets iteratively matches the user's stated preference. On the claims side, the strongest available outcome is a feasibility label on correlated training fields plus reused development fields, and the bundle never promises more. The one place the label could quietly overstate is the fixture0 aggregate (E1); with that bound, the claim ceiling and the evidence match.

**Bottom line:** launch after E1 (declare the 12-field gate), E2 (memory accounting), and E3 (one augmentation transform test). No other changes; no gate ladder.
